problem: Nintendo wanted to reach people who did not play games.
title: Nintendo launches the Wii aimed at casual players at a lower price
context: Rivals competed on graphics power and price premiums with the Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3.
decision_made: Build a console around a motion controller, price it at about $250 and market it to older and less experienced players.
action_taken: Launched in November 2006; about 70 percent of its US launch marketing reportedly targeted older and less experienced gamers.
observed_outcome: Wii sold more than three million units by the end of 2006 and roughly 101 million over its life, becoming Nintendo's best-selling home console until the Switch passed it.
lessons: Competing on a different dimension, such as accessibility and price, can beat rivals on raw power.
limitations: The marketing split and executive quotes come from secondary reports. Later sales decline for the Wii and the effect on software profits were not checked here.

claims.claim_text: Nintendo priced the Wii well below its rivals and marketed it to casual and older players.
The Wii sold more than three million units worldwide by the end of 2006.
